findings.problem: Requiring the measurements to come from an ambient basis excludes arbitrary rational linear functionals and redundant coordinate systems. The construction uses only that each coordinate preserves zero and scalar multiplication; neither independence nor completeness of the ambient coordinates is needed.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a general core statement with the following signature, retaining the existing theorem as its specialization at ℓ := e.coord:

{ι α β L : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
[AddCommGroup L] [Module ℚ L]
(ℓ : ι → L →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ)
(P Q : Submodule ℚ L) (hQP : Q ≤ P)
(a : Basis α ℚ Q) (b : Basis β ℚ P)
(q : ℚ) {H K : ℕ} (hH : 1 ≤ H) (hK : 1 ≤ K)
(hq : RationalHeightLE q K)
(ha : ∀ j k, RationalHeightLE (ℓ k (a j : L)) H)
(hb : ∀ j k, RationalHeightLE (ℓ k (b j : L)) H) :
∃ c : Basis (Fin (finrank ℚ (scaledPairLayer P Q q))) ℚ (scaledPairLayer P Q q),
  ∀ j k, RationalHeightLE (ℓ k (c j).val.1) (H * K) ∧
    RationalHeightLE (ℓ k (c j).val.2) (H * K)

Use the same mapped product basis and reindexing. Its vectors are (a j, 0) and (q • b j, b j). Apply LinearMap.map_zero and LinearMap.map_smul, followed by rationalHeightLE_zero, RationalHeightLE.mono and RationalHeightLE.mul exactly as in the present proof. No injectivity assumption or finite index type ι is necessary. Empty measurement families, zero subspaces and q = 0 remain valid under the retained height-positivity assumptions.
findings.benefit: Users can transfer height bounds for selected functionals or existing linear coordinate maps without constructing an ambient basis or converting their bounds to basis coordinates. The repository already exposes coordinate maps as linear maps, so this supports a concrete existing representation while preserving the current API.
